description: An oscillator built on tropical additive synthesis: five sines are offset against each other and the quietest of them at each instant is what comes out

params.text: Sets the pitch in whole octaves, three either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Detunes that oscillator by up to 10Hz either way from the harmonic it is set to, which beats it against the rest
Raises or lowers that oscillator before the lowest of the five is taken, from -1 to 1; raising it keeps it out of the result for more of the cycle and lowering it brings it in
Shifts the whole output up or down by up to 2, which moves it against the ±5V the output is scaled to
Chooses which harmonics the five oscillators take: FULL gives the first five, EVEN the fundamental with the second, fourth, sixth and eighth, ODD it with the third, fifth, seventh and ninth

inputs.text: Sets the pitch, an octave per volt, added to the OCTAVE knob and held within four octaves either side of C4
Adds to that oscillator's detuning, one hertz per volt
Adds to that oscillator's level, a fifth per volt, with the total clamped between -1 and 1

outputs.text: The lowest of the five oscillators at each instant, plus the DC offset, scaled to ±5V

notes: the mixer is a minimum rather than a sum, which is what makes this tropical: adding a level before a minimum does the work that multiplying does in ordinary additive synthesis.
a detune that would drive an oscillator's frequency to zero or below is refused, and that oscillator stays at the last frequency it was given.
the DC offset has no CV input of its own.
the method is from a 2018 paper by Cristiano Bocci and Giorgio Sancristoforo, named on the panel.

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
